722 white students enrolled in Van Buren County schools in 2024-25
G. M. Myers
Van Buren County schools enrolled 722 white students in the 2024-25 school year, a decline of 1.6% from the previous year, according to the Iowa Department of Education.
Data showed that Van Buren County enrolled 765 students in the 2024-25 school year. White students made up 94.4% of that total, the most represented ethnicity in the county.
Of the county's three schools, Van Buren County Community Middle & High School had the largest white student enrollment in the 2024-25 school year, with 336.
Iowa's certified K-12 enrollment declined slightly in the 2025-26 school year, according to the Iowa Department of Education. Total certified enrollment across public and accredited nonpublic schools fell 0.9% to 515,221 students. Public district and charter school enrollment declined 1.53% to 473,329 students, while accredited nonpublic school enrollment rose 6.4% to 41,892.
It also reported that 41,044 students used Students First Education Savings Accounts at accredited nonpublic schools as of the Oct. 1 certified enrollment date.
